title: 1.4.6 Which Level Fits?
description: Five multiple-choice questions on levels of abstraction and picking a language level against a deadline. Checked instantly.

questions.question: A small team has eight weeks to ship a working web app. One member wants a low-level language because the program will run faster. Which level should they choose?
options: Low-level
Neither: the level makes no difference to how long it takes to write
Whichever one runs fastest, always
High-level
questions.explanation: High-level. The deadline is the binding constraint, and high-level languages are faster to write.

questions.question: What is the scarce resource for that team?
options: Machine speed
Memory
Programmer time
Disk space
questions.explanation: Eight weeks is what they are short of. The right level is the one that spends the scarce resource most carefully.

questions.question: What does a language's "level of abstraction" mean?
options: How difficult the language is for a beginner to learn
How much machine detail the language hides from you
How many built-in commands the language has
How recently the language was invented
questions.explanation: How far the language sits from the hardware. The detail still happens: you are just not the one describing it.

questions.question: What is the team trading away by choosing a high-level language?
options: Some run speed, and direct control over the hardware
Nothing: high-level languages are better in every way
The ability to build a web app at all
The ability to use variables
questions.explanation: Every choice on this scale has a cost. Here it is a little run speed and the fine-grained control.

questions.question: Which job is the better argument for a low-level language?
options: Building a school website over one term
Writing a program that adds two numbers together
Any project with a tight deadline
Writing the code that drives a hard disk, where control over the hardware is the point
questions.explanation: When hardware control IS the job, low-level earns its cost. Neither end of the scale wins in general.
